candidate_records.name: Abbott Lodge
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010182 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1820. NIAH records yellow Flemish-bond brick, moulded granite plinth and string course over coursed limestone basement walls, diminishing gauged window openings, timber sliding sashes, an Ionic doorcase and spearheaded railings. Basement area is shared with and accessed from No.86. A recent single-storey mews building to the rear spans a double plot shared with No.88.

candidate_records.name: O'Carroll Construction
candidate_records.address: 33 Gardiner Street Lower / Deverell Place, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010186 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Corner-sited end-of-terrace two-bay four-storey house over raised basement, built c.1840, with a single-storey rendered wing fronting Deverell Place, built c.1900. Built as one of a pair with No.34. NIAH records yellow Flemish-bond brick, calp-stone basement, wrought-iron balconettes, Ionic doorcase, decorative railings, a rare carved sandstone water tank, restored interior plasterwork and timber joinery, and a dog-leg timber stair. The retained rear screen wall known as Queen's Wall was built c.1900 for Queen Victoria's visit and includes Doric pilasters, frieze and cornice. The appraisal identifies the house and rear screen wall as architecturally important.

spatial_and_identity_cautions: Nos.87 and 88 are separately registered houses. Their shared basement access arrangement and double-width rear mews structure are relationships, not a reason to merge the two street-front registrations.
Nos.89 and 90 are separately registered houses despite the shared commercial name and restaurant/guesthouse operation. Do not treat the operating guesthouse as a single architectural registration.
No.33 is a separate corner-sited house at Deverell Place, built as one of a pair with No.34 (registration 50010187). The pair relationship does not merge the two registrations.
The Queen's Wall is a retained rear screen-wall feature described as part of the No.33 record; do not create an extra object without independent object-level evidence or a separate registration.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved as raw values because the page does not label their CRS. Do not interpret them as EPSG:2157 or overwrite official CSV coordinates.
NIAH descriptions of use, condition and alterations are survey-time source statements, not present-day field verification.
